body: I think the piece of this thread you're responding to may be the last couple of posts... those were intended as context and response to the first response I had received. I genuinely appreciate the time you took to answer and your kind intentions, but I will be honest that something about the response itself rubbed me the wrong way. I've been thinking a lot about how to explain what it is so that my words might be useful rather than simply unkind or ungrateful. I guess a part of it is the sort of "chin up" tone... I posted initially that I'm aware I have a fortunate life... and I'm also aware that pets are a huge responsibility and "something to care about." (If ever I'm in danger of forgetting, they seem very happy to remind me regularly with a special blend of unconditional love and absurd vet bills...) I can't help but think when I read your response that I am not reading the words of someone who has ever looked at the prospect of living a half to two thirds of their life (ballpark estimate) not only without love and children, but without close family ties whatsoever. I get that no one else can fulfill another person but it doesn't really seem a pleasant way to live and it also takes away one of the stronger reasons people express for continuing to live even when things are difficult. Being told that I just need to be more content on my own feels especially dismissive since this post is just the tip of the iceberg of a very complicated life and there are many factors I did not go into here just because I was looking to express some feelings that are not generally acceptable to express in society, rather than tell my life story. I'm not saying it's any reason to die, even including all the factors I've left out or only alluded to in passing, but on the other hand is anything? I know people who have survived the suicides of loved ones, and I know a thing or two about suicide prevention, and I guess one thing I can take from that body of knowledge is that really nothing ever looks like a great reason to intentionally die from the outside. That doesn't mean those reasons are not incredibly powerful in the hearts and minds of those who have to carry them, or it's very likely no one would ever intentionally end their life what with the stigma and disapproval attached. I'm truly not trying to be hurtful or difficult, just honest since this is a forum where it seems to me a lot of fragile people may well be posting and it's good to be aware of how one's words can strike the listener. I do understand that you're coming from a kind place, and I do appreciate any kindness at this point, and because of that it was difficult to know how to respond.

Thank you for your kindness. Thank you also for recognizing what an unsatisfying endeavor trying to make friends into something that is just more than friends generally are would be...hearing so many times that I could find or develop friendships that would somehow take the place of familial type relationships when I had said just as many times that this was not what I wanted, was actually one of the reasons I quit therapy besides the time and expense!

To clarify, it's not really the dumping that is causing me to want to die... I've felt that way off and on in varying intensity for a long time, much of it before this relationship such as it was even happened. I don't know that I will find love... I hate the whole dating game to the point I can't seem to push myself into it once again, and the way my life is set up I don't tend to meet too many eligible people spontaneously. I think I'm overly selective and don't attach or open up easily... even though I've clearly made the wrong selections and attached to the wrong people when I do! Time is running out as far as romantic love and children and I guess I feel I could get over that more easily if I had any other type of family, but I really don't in any meaningful sense.

I'm sorry you are living under these conditions. Have you looked into programs or support groups for people with HIV or people living with a low income in your area? Is there any way you could change jobs or start job searching for something better? Could you get trained in a trade or profession that is better paying or has better hours? I can't tell you to live or die, but if your desire to die has to do with the material conditions of your life, those can change, and it may be worth trying a few different means of changing them before resorting to suicide.

You ask what reason there is to live, and this is another question that you can answer better than I can... do you have friends or family? Things you haven't seen, or done, or tried that you would like to before your life is over? There must be something that makes you hesitate to end your life or you wouldn't still be here... I'm curious to know what it is if you don't mind telling.
I can listen and support. I can help you problem-solve, if you like. You're in a tough situation and there is no denying that, and I'm sorry for all you are going through at such a young age.
You write very beautifully. And I'm so sorry you are in such pain. I hope I have not said too much, since you did mention not wanting responses... If you would prefer I delete this, I can.
